$comment: TEST FIXTURE -- the TEST-REPORT verb's repository. It declares no 'test-report' verb anywhere, on purpose: that verb runs project.verbs.<lane>.test and reads THAT row's artifacts, because a repository which has said how its tests run has said enough. Ten lanes, one per answer the verb has to have. Separate from shu-repo because that one is the EXECUTOR's fixture and declares no test artifacts -- folding the two together would delete the 'declares none' case. Not shipped; see ../../README.md.

blocked.why: An unsatisfiable precondition, so the executor refuses at 2 having started nothing -- while a real report sits on disk at this lane's declared artifact. Nen must report NOTHING parsed there: the file is certainly not this invocation's.

test.why: The lane the parse is proved on end to end. `artifacts` names the file the runner writes; nen parses the FIRST entry whose format it recognises and never searches for one.
DECLARES NO ARTIFACTS. The run succeeds and nen has nothing to parse: the refusal names the field to declare and lists the formats it reads.

THE TWO-STEP SHAPE THIS FAMILY MEANS BY 'declared': the result bundle is a directory in a proprietary layout, and the only supported way to read one is the vendor's own extraction tool -- so the DECLARATION runs it as a second step and names the JSON it writes. nen never spawns an extraction of its own; it reads the file this repository said it would produce.

A DIRECTORY ARTIFACT: this runner writes one XML file per suite, so the declaration names the directory it writes them into. nen reads every *.xml under it, in sorted order, and merges them into one report -- there is no shell here and no glob is expanded.

THE ORDINARY SHAPE, plus the trap. A test verb writes several things and only one is a machine-readable report: `notes.md` is passed over because nen recognises no format for it, and `bin/app` is passed over because an artifact whose NAME states a format nen reads is chosen before one that merely has no extension. Choosing in one pass would parse the binary and refuse a lane that declared exactly what it was asked for.
A declared report that is not on disk after a successful run: exit 1 naming the path, because the runner wrote it somewhere else or wrote nothing.

A directory artifact holding an XML file that is not a test report. Every *.xml under a directory artifact is read, so one nen does not recognise refuses the whole read by name rather than being skipped past -- reading half a tree and reporting a total for it is the failure this verb must not have.

A directory artifact with no *.xml anywhere under it: exit 1 saying so, because a directory nen reads as a tree of XML and finds none in is a declaration pointing above (or beside) the directory the runner writes into.

THE TRAP THIS VERB IS ARRANGED AROUND. Its precondition can never be satisfied, so no step runs -- and its declared artifact is a real, parseable report (the `web` lane's). A run that started nothing must parse nothing, whatever is on disk.

build.why: A lane with a build and NO test. 'nen shu test-report' answers exit 4 in the declaration's own terms, in every form -- including --from-artifacts, because the artifact list is a property of the invocation this lane does not have.
